title: Prologue
body:
## Prologue — The Tide Book

The tide book was kept by hand for ninety years, and every page of it was wrong in the same direction.

title: The Drowned Rows
summary: Maren arrives and finds the orchard flooded.
body:
## Chapter 1 — The Drowned Rows

Maren came up the lane at slack water, when the ditches stood full and still.

The lower rows were under a hand's depth of brine. Pell was already there, hauling a net through the trees as if the orchard were a harbour.

---

<!-- note: check the tide times against chapter 3 -->

Ilse's house had kept its shutters closed. Maren stood on the porch a while before she tried the door, and it opened.

---

### The Kitchen

The kettle was warm. Somebody had been there that morning, and had left in a hurry, and had wanted her to know it.

She could hear the pumps from here.

title: The Key
body:
## Chapter 2 — The Key

The key was colder than the morning. She turned it over twice before she understood it was hers.

***

Tobin Reyes was waiting at the port with the look of a man who had rehearsed an apology. [[tobin-reyes|Tobin]] had not changed his coat in a decade.

He said the harbour office still had her father's survey, and that the survey disagreed with the water.

title: Low Water
body:
## Chapter 3 — Low Water

By evening the water had gone out of the lower rows and left a white crust on the bark.

Maren walked the rows with the brass key in her pocket and counted the trees that still bore fruit [^cite:harbour-survey].

title: The Tidewardens
body:
## Chapter 4 — The Tidewardens

The Tidewardens met in the net loft, under a ceiling of drying cork floats.

___

Afterwards Ilse's letter was read aloud, twice, and nobody looked at Maren while it was.

A line added behind the cache.
